Cross-country spillovers from the regional core (stage 2d)

Six entities, three policy rules — the most seed-reproducible battery in this project, and the one shock that does not work

1. What this is

The battery reports/stage2c_spillovers.qmd runs, re-run on the stage 2d system: six entities (de, fr, it, us, cn, reu), stage 2c’s equations unchanged, k = 46 against T = 78, df = 32.

That df is the reason to read this report. Stage 2b and 2c both ran at df = 22 and CLAUDE.md records what that cost: re-running the same battery on the same fit at a different seed moved an off-diagonal spillover cell by 0.35pp on average for stage 2b, flipping the sign of 7–10 cells out of 30. Most of what anyone wanted to conclude from that matrix was smaller than its own noise. Stage 2d has half the equations and ten more degrees of freedom, and §3 measures what that buys.

koma has no impulse-response function, so every number here is the difference between two koma::forecast() calls — one unconditional, one restricted — paired by common random numbers (the same set.seed() immediately before each), so the difference isolates the shock rather than koma’s call-to-call forecast noise. Three shocks:

  • Demand: +1pp on one entity’s GDP growth in the first forecast quarter only, after which GDP evolves under the model’s own dynamics.
  • Monetary: +100bp held on a policy rate for four quarters.
  • Oil: a +50% level shock to oil_price, which is exogenous and therefore cannot use restrictions at all — it needs a whole shocked copy of the fit.
The exogenous series had to be carried past the fit’s native forecast end first. koma silently shortens a horizon it cannot supply, so without this the battery would have returned fewer quarters than it claimed.

spillover_sanity_checks() on the seed-A battery.
check ok detail
own effect exceeds every cross-country effect TRUE 6/6 countries: own > max|cross|
monetary contraction is negative for GDP and prices everywhere FALSE GDP peak negative: 6/6 | prices peak negative: 1/6
spillover magnitude correlates with bilateral trade weight FALSE Spearman rho = 0.138 (pass threshold: > 0.3)

Own effect dominates in 1 of the checks — 6 of 6 entities, the same clean result stage 2c reached and better than stage 2b’s 7 of 11, where Austria’s two-hop artefact broke it.

Two features of the matrix are worth naming because they are properties of the partition rather than of the estimator.

China’s row is an order of magnitude smaller than everyone else’s. A +1pp Chinese demand shock delivers 0.158pp to Germany and 0.056pp to the US, against 0.385–0.964pp for the intra-European pairs. That is what the trade weights say it should be: China’s bilateral weight on Germany is 3.4% and on the euro area as a whole 4.4%, because 78% of Chinese goods trade is with economies this model does not contain. The asymmetry is real — China’s column is larger than its row, so Europe reaches China more than China reaches Europe — and it is a direct consequence of using observed IMF DOTS weights for the Chinese row instead of the reciprocal approximation, which would have put 56% of Chinese trade inside the euro area and inverted this result.

reu behaves like a large country, not like a residual. Its own effect (1.398) is the largest on the diagonal and its outward spillovers are comparable to Germany’s, which is what a bloc holding roughly a third of euro-area GDP should look like.

3. The seed placebo — and this is the headline

Before reporting that any of the above differs from stage 2b or 2c, the battery has to clear its own noise floor. 4 source entities were re-run at a second seed on the same fit, and the two matrices compared cell by cell.

Seed-to-seed movement of an off-diagonal spillover cell, same fit, different seed. Stage 2b and 2c figures from CLAUDE.md.
System Mean |seed A - seed B| Max Off-diagonal sign flips
stage 2b (df = 22) 0.350 1.850 7-10 of 30
stage 2c (df = 22) 0.119 0.356 1 of 44
stage 2d (df = 32) 0.108 0.273 0 of 20

0 sign flips out of 20, a mean gap of 0.108pp and a worst case of 0.273pp. Stage 2c already improved on stage 2b by a factor of three; stage 2d improves on stage 2c again, and for the first time no off-diagonal cell changes sign when only the seed changes.

This is the strongest result in the stage-2d work, and it is strong precisely because it is a measurement of the noise rather than a claim made on top of it. It is also the concrete payoff of the re-partition: collapsing seven countries into a bloc was justified in reports/stage2d_regional_core.qmd on degrees of freedom alone, and this is what those ten extra degrees of freedom actually buy — a spillover matrix whose individual cells can be read, which neither of its predecessors’ could be.

4. The monetary shock

4.1 The euro-area rule behaves

Cumulative and peak responses to the euro-area tightening, at both seeds.
Entity GDP cum. (seed A) GDP cum. (seed B) GDP peak (A) Prices cum. (A)
CN -0.025 0.036 -0.010 0.000
DE -1.322 -1.226 -0.297 0.544
FR -0.505 -0.360 -0.084 0.046
IT -1.027 -0.768 -0.268 0.324
REU -0.613 -0.296 -0.116 0.185
US -0.131 0.116 -0.030 0.002

GDP is correctly signed and the transmission is orderly. Every entity’s peak GDP response is negative, the euro-area members most of all (-1.32pp cumulative for Germany, -1.03 for Italy), and the long rate tracks the policy rate essentially one-for-one, as the spread identity imposes. The two entities outside the euro area show the smallest responses and are not robust to the seed — the US goes from -0.131 to +0.116 and China from -0.025 to +0.036, crossing zero in both cases. Read those two as indistinguishable from nothing, which is the economically sensible answer anyway.

Prices are still wrong-signed, and that is inherited, not new. Only 1 of 6 entities show a negative price peak under a tightening. Stage 2c reported exactly this failure across all eleven countries and diagnosed it: the policy rate’s route into GDP is dominated by the horizon-1 simultaneity echo rather than a lagged demand channel, so the Phillips curve is fed a positive output impulse in the same quarter the rate rises. The re-partition does not touch that mechanism, so it does not fix it. The oil shock in §5 is the control that localises the fault to the policy-rate route rather than to the price block itself.

A sustained restriction makes some draws fail outright. koma drops them by subsetting the list, recording nothing about which index, so scenario_diff() refuses to difference legs of unequal length; failed_restriction_draws() recovers the indices by tracing koma:::forecast_draw() and the baseline is re-paired against exactly those.

posterior draws attempted 1000
draws that failed the restriction 25
share 2.5%

4.2 The Chinese policy rate shock does not work

China’s own response to +100bp on cn_policy_rate, by horizon.
variable h1 h2 h3 h4 h5 h6 h7 h8
cn_policy_rate 1.006 0.994 1.003 0.991 0.745 0.626 0.421 0.380
cn_long_rate 1.482 1.590 1.724 1.733 1.435 1.251 0.990 0.871
cn_prices 1.375 0.798 0.733 0.460 0.296 0.122 0.091 0.035
cn_domestic_demand 7.391 0.012 0.833 0.183 0.025 -0.001 -0.034 0.009
cn_gdp 6.669 0.267 0.953 0.219 0.033 0.016 -0.002 0.012

This is a negative result and it should be read as one. A +100bp Chinese tightening raises Chinese GDP by 6.67pp in the first quarter and by 8.17pp cumulatively — the wrong sign, and far too large.

The mechanism is identifiable and it is not a bug in the shock. cn_policy_rate has its own Taylor rule, and the restriction forces that rate a full point above where the rule says it should be. The solver has to make the rule’s own arguments consistent with that, and the rule’s loadings are 0.152 on prices and 0.015 on GDP — so it takes a very large move in Chinese output and prices to justify a one-point rate rise. That is the entire response: it lands at horizon 1 and decays to nothing by horizon 3. It is a within-quarter accounting adjustment in the rule, not transmission.

Nothing pushes back the other way, because China’s demand channel is empty: cn_domestic_demand’s loading on cn_long_rate is -0.0188, with a 90% interval straddling zero. And that in turn traces to the data: cn_long_rate is spliced over 45% of the estimation window (OECD’s Chinese 10-year yield starts only 2014Q1), so before 2014 it moves exactly like the three-month interbank rate and carries no independent term-premium variation for the equation to identify against.

The euro-area rule does not have this problem because ea_policy_rate responds to ea_gdp and ea_prices, which are identities over four entities — the adjustment is spread across the whole area rather than loaded onto one country.

Do not use cn_policy_rate as a monetary experiment in this system. If a Chinese monetary channel is what you need, the place to start is stage2d_config(spread_countries = setdiff(stage2d_countries(), "cn")), which drops the spliced long rate and lets Chinese demand load the complete, unspliced IRSTCI policy rate directly.

5. The oil shock

Cumulative response to a +50% oil price shock.
Entity Prices cum. (pp) GDP cum. (pp)
CN 0.798 -0.031
DE 2.591 -1.031
FR 1.996 -0.466
IT 1.447 -0.786
REU 2.623 -0.634
US 2.018 -0.388

Correctly signed in 6 of 6, at 0.8–2.6pp cumulative — the same result stage 2c got, and the control that matters for §4. The price block responds sensibly to a cost shock and perversely to a policy rate, which localises the monetary failure to the policy rate’s route into the system rather than to the price equations themselves.

China’s price response (0.80pp) is the smallest, which is plausible: Chinese consumer prices are heavily food-weighted and administered energy pricing damps pass-through.

6. What still fails

The trade-weight check.
check ok detail
spillover magnitude correlates with bilateral trade weight FALSE Spearman rho = 0.138 (pass threshold: > 0.3)

Spillover magnitude still does not correlate with bilateral trade weight strongly enough to pass. The Spearman correlation is NA against a 0.3 bar — comparable to stage 2b’s 0.141 and worse than stage 2c’s 0.292. With six entities there are only 30 ordered pairs, so this statistic is itself thin; but it is reported as a failure rather than explained away.

The explosive share climbs to roughly 35–48% by horizon 8, which is materially better than stage 2b/2c’s ~50% and stage 3b’s 67% but is still the binding constraint on how far this battery can be pushed. It is why every headline in this report is a cumulative median over surviving draws and why §3 exists.

7. Verdict

Check Result
Own effect dominates 6 / 6 — better than stage 2b (7/11), matching stage 2c
Seed reproducibility best in the project — 0 sign flips of 20, mean gap 0.108pp
Monetary → GDP (euro area) correctly signed, robust to the seed for the four EA entities
Monetary → prices still wrong-signed, inherited from stage 2c and not addressed by the re-partition
Monetary → China’s own rule does not work — a horizon-1 rule adjustment, not transmission
Oil → prices correctly signed 6 / 6
Trade-weight correlation fails at NA

Use this system for demand spillovers between the euro area, the US and China, where the matrix is now reproducible enough to read cell by cell, and for cost-push experiments. Do not use it for a monetary experiment on China, and treat any price response to a policy rate — in this stage or its predecessors — as unresolved.
